newsitem.title: JAPAN: OLYMPICS-STRONG DOLLAR BOOSTS NAGANO OLYMPICS INCOME.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-STRONG DOLLAR BOOSTS NAGANO OLYMPICS INCOME.

text.p: Extra income from a strengthening dollar will be spent on new television technology and improved computerised results systems, the chief organiser of next years Nagano Winter Olympics said on Friday.
"We want to ensure that they will be high-tech Games," said Makoto Kobayashi, director general of the Nagano Olympic Organising Committee (NAOC).
Total operating expenses for the Games will increase to 103 billion yen ($936 million) from 94.5 billion yen ($859 million) mostly due to the fall of the yen against the dollar, he said.

A newly adopted 110 yen to the dollar exchange rate for the dollar-based price of television rights and international sponsorship contracts would yield an extra 6.6 billion yen ($60 million) in income, he said.
NAOC abandoned the 95 yen to the dollar rate used in its previous budget released last March after the dollar recently soared to its highest levels in four years.
NAOC will earn $310.3 million for television rights alone, almost a third of its income.
Organisers also plan to install an additional seven large-screen televisions, so that all 15 venues will be equipped, he said.
Provisions were also being made in the budget to safeguard against any possible strengthening of the yen, Kobayashi said, without elaborating.
